body:
I have added a workaround: at the moment the draco-support is disabled as the default. At this moment I don't have an idea why the error comes up for VCS2019.

I will have to dig deeper. Thanks for your help. I am wondering why this issue ways not detected by our CI-chain.
Ok, thanks for taking time to look into it! I have no idea what's going on, but it's interesting that the issue is not reproduced with VS2017.

The problem seems to be that the `draco_features.h` file is being copied to `build/draco/`, but the generated MSVC project expects it to be in `build/vendor/assimp/draco/`

I'm not sure where those two paths come from, the upstream draco cmakelists are rather complex.

The MSVC2017 project doesn't actually build either, the apparent success appears to be an MSVC2017 UI bug.

Looked into this a bit further. There's a few options to fix this:
1. Add `${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}` (`build` in your example) to the include path for the assimp projects.
2. Place `draco_features.h` into `build/vendor/assimp/contrib/draco/`
3. Place `draco_features.h` into `build/vendor/assimp/include/assimp/draco/`

Option 1 is simplest as it doesn't require any changes or patches to upstream, however it is polluting the folder tree of the top-level project that's consuming assimp.

I think I prefer option 2 as that's consistent with zlib, what do you think?

Thanks for figuring that out! I think I agree with your thoughts on option 1. It feels like it violates modularization of the library a little bit?  I don't think I have enough experience to suggest a preference between 2 and 3.
